full_text: The 3rd bowl tasted like rot. I couldn't feel my hands anymore. The wolf bead had already reached my chest. Lucien stood at the end of the bed and watched me go. 7 pups, all high-ranking blood. That's enough. I tried to speak. Nothing came out. You were never the one I wanted, Vivienne. His voice didn't waver. You threw yourself at me. I let it happen. That's all this ever was. I wanted to scream. I wanted to tear him apart, but my body was already gone. You've served your purpose. He set the empty bowl down. Rest now. My heartbeat slowed. Then nothing. I opened my eyes in my mother's sitting room I came back. I pressed my hands flat against my thighs and breathed. My mother was holding a contract across the room, a mating bond contract, sealed with the Bloodmoon Pack crest. The name line was blank. The Valises' heir sent this earlier this morning, Viviana. Is it you he's asking for? Lucien sat across from her, same face, eyes wide. Same steady eyes, like none of it had ever happened. I can marry Vivian. I don't mind. I don't mind. 7 years, 7 children, 3 bowls of wolfsbane. No. Silence. Viviana, you've wanted this since you were 12. I was a kid. I didn't know any better. Lucien looked at me, that calm, unreleasable stare I used to think meant he was hiding something tender. Now I knew better. I also have someone. He'll be here soon with his own contract. My mother's head snapped toward Aria. Aria had been quiet in the corner this whole time. Now she shook her head hard. Same. I'm not available either. My mother turned back to Lucien with a tight smile. I'm so sorry. It seems both my daughters have prior commitments. Perhaps another pack? No. Lucien stood. The Alpha aura rolled off him slow and deliberate, pressing into every corner of the room. The woman I marry comes from the Coldwield family. His voice left no room for argument. That's not changing. He picked up the contract and dropped it on the table. The sound cut through the silence like a blade. You have 3 days. Decide who it is. Nobody moved. If you can't choose... He straightened his jacket. I'll take it to the Alpha King. One word from him and it becomes a royal decree. There won't be a choice after that. He walked out without looking back. The door hadn't finished closing before Aria grabbed my wrist and pulled me down the hall. She shut us into my bedroom and pressed her back against the door. Her face was white, I'll tell you something, but you have to promise not to feel guilty, she said. I went still. Aria... Promise me first. Something cold settled in my chest. I promise. She didn't look at me when she spoke. In another life, she said quietly, you gave me the contract. You told me Lucien loved me. You stepped aside... I couldn't breathe. He didn't love me. Her voice was flat, controlled. He kept me locked in a room. He said the only thing I was good for was my Moonveil voice. He made me sing for him every night. She paused. Every time I complained, he hurt me. Aria... She finally looked at me. Her eyes were dry. That was somehow worse. He had my limbs severed so I couldn't shift. He took my eyes. He left me my voice because that was the only part of me he wanted. I couldn't speak. I made it back because a servant broke the lock. I didn't last 2 months after that. I crossed the room and pulled her into a hug. She went stiff for a second, then her arms came up and held on. We stayed like that for a long moment. I pulled back, looked at her seriously. I have something to tell you too. I told her about everything I'd been through, including that I had been reborn too. Aria's expression turned puzzled after learning the truth. So what do we do? We tell Mom everything. My mother didn't speak while we talked. She
